Can Section 8 companies make profits? Yes, Section 8 companies can make profits through various means, like investments, donations, funding, etc. Profits generated by these companies must be used only to promote their charitable objectives. What is the difference between an NGO and a Section 8 company? An NGO is an independent organization with the various social objectives, like charity for educational and health, etc. A Section 8 Company is a non-profit organization formed to promote various social objectives in the field of commerce, education, and social welfare. Can NRIs/Foreign Nationals work as Directors in a Section 8 Company? Yes, NRIs or any Foreign National can serve as a Director in a Section 8 Company after obtaining a Director Identification Number (DIN). Who grants the license for a Section 8 company? The Central government entrusted the responsibility of Section 8 Company registration to the Registrars of Companies in their respective jurisdictions Can a One Person Company (OPC) be converted into a Section 8 company? No, as per the Companies Incorporation (Rules), 2014, it prohibits the incorporation or conversion of an OPC into a Section 8 company.

sections.heading: Section 7
paragraphs: A Section 8 Company is a kind of company established to promote social activities in various fields, like education, social welfare, environmental protection, arts, sports, and many more. Section 8 Companies are governed by the Companies Act, 2013.

The primary goal of a Section 8 Company registration in India is to encourage charity in various kinds of social activities, trade, arts, commerce, education, charity, environmental protection, sports, research, agriculture and social welfare. You will need a minimum of two directors to register a Section 8 Company. Criteria of minimum paid-up capital is not applied in the registration of Section 8 Companies.
There are various benefits of Section 8 Company registration. Some of them are discussed here:

Tax Exemption: Section 8 companies registered under section 12AA of the Income Tax Act enjoy 100% income tax exemption. It is a significant benefit for Section 8 companies as the profits generated by these companies are non-taxable.
Zero Stamp Duty: You don’t have to pay stamp for Section 8 company registration in India.
No Minimum Capital: You need not to maintain a minimum capital requirement for Section 8 Company registration.

Separate Legal Entity: Section 8 companies have status of distinct legal entities like other companies. It enables these companies to own property, sign contracts, and take legal actions in their name.
Increased Credibility: Non-profit nature of the Section 8 company registration in India enhances their trustworthiness and credibility.
Eligible for Grants: They are eligible to get grants from the government and international organizations.
The following documents are needed to complete the registration process for a Section 8 company in India:
Articles of Association (AOA) and Memorandum of Association (MOA) of the company
Proof of office address, like a copy of utility bills like electricity, water, or gas bill
A resolution passed by the sponsored company
Consent of Nominee (INC-3)
Residential and identity proof of nominees and subscribers are needed for Section 8 company registration online.
